title: Review: Single-slit diffraction; Reflection and refraction; Scalars and vectors; Newton's first law and equilibrium; Moments and static equilibrium; Systems and centre of mass
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MS05-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; D02-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; W04-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; W08-1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D02-1#N.11, D07-1#N.2, D08-1#N.5a, MS05-1#N.4, W04-1#N.6a, W08-1#N.12, D02-1#N.2, D08-1#N.2, MS05-1#N.13, W04-1#N.9a, W08-1#N.7c, D02-1#N.9. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Resultant
items.clue: Runs from the first tail to the last tip when arrows are drawn tip to tail.

items.label: Terminal velocity
items.clue: Constant value a skydiver's downward motion settles at once drag equals weight.

items.label: Ray
items.clue: Line perpendicular to the wavefronts, showing the direction the energy travels.

items.label: Wavelength
items.clue: Quantity the gap width must be comparable with for strong spreading; about 0.3 to 3 m for speech.

questions.stem: Which of the following objects is in translational equilibrium?

options.text: A ball at the top of its flight, momentarily at rest
A car rounding a curve on a level road at a constant speed
A puck slowing down on rough ice after a stick stops pushing it
A crate riding up a straight conveyor at a steady 2 m s⁻¹

questions.explanation: Its speed and direction are both constant, so its velocity is constant and the net force on it is zero: friction from the belt, up the slope, balances the component of its weight down the slope, and the normal force balances the rest.

questions.stem: A cylindrical rod is made of a 0.50 m aluminium section joined end to end to a 0.50 m steel section of the same diameter. Each section is uniform, and the steel section has the greater mass. How does the location of the rod's centre of mass compare with the rod's midpoint?

options.text: It is at the midpoint, since the rod's shape is symmetric about that point.
It is on the aluminium side of the midpoint, nearer the lighter section.
It is at the centre of the steel section, the more massive part.
It lies between the midpoint and the centre of the steel section.

questions.stem: A uniform beam of length 5.0 m and weight 400 N rests horizontally on two supports, one at each end, P and Q. A person of weight 600 N stands on the beam 1.0 m from Q. What is the upward force from support P?
questions.explanation: Taking moments about Q: F_P × 5.0 = 400 × 2.5 + 600 × 1.0 = 1600 N m, so F_P = 320 N.

questions.stem: A hiker walks 5 m east and then 9 m west along a straight path. Student 1 takes east as the positive direction; Student 2 takes west as the positive direction. Each finds the hiker's resultant displacement as a signed component. Which statement correctly compares their results?

options.text: Only Student 1 can be right, as east has to be the positive direction.
Student 1 gets −4 m and Student 2 gets +4 m, and both results mean 4 m west.
Both get +4 m, by subtracting the smaller distance from the larger.
Both get 14 m, since the two walks simply add to give the resultant.

questions.stem: The refractive index of a certain plastic is 1.5. Which statement correctly describes what this value means?

options.text: Light travels 1.5 times as fast in the plastic as in a vacuum.
The plastic's density is 1.5 times the density of water.
A ray entering from air is bent to 1/1.5 of its angle of incidence.
Light travels 1.5 times as fast in a vacuum as it does in the plastic.

questions.stem: Sea waves reach a harbour wall with a 20 m wide entrance. A boat is moored behind the wall, well to one side of the entrance. On day 1 the waves have a wavelength of 20 m; on day 2, 2.0 m, with the same amplitude. On which day is the boat rocked more, and why?

options.text: Day 1: the wavelength is about the width of the gap, so the waves spread widely.
Day 2: shorter waves have a higher frequency, so they carry more energy around the wall.
Neither: the gap is the same width both days, and the gap alone sets the spreading.
Day 2: shorter waves fit through the gap more easily, so more of them pass behind it.

questions.stem: A space probe is so far from any star or planet that the forces exerted on it are negligible. Its engines fire briefly and then shut off. Which statement describes the probe's motion after the engines have shut off?

options.text: It slows down and stops, as all moving objects do in time.
It slows down as the force from the engine firing is used up.
It moves in a straight line at a constant speed.
It stops almost at once, as no force now pushes it forward.

questions.stem: A mechanic pulls with a 20 N force on the end of a tool handle, 0.25 m from the centre of a nut. The force is in the plane of the handle's turn, but at 30° to the handle instead of at 90°. What is the turning effect of the force about the centre of the nut?

options.text: 5.0 N m
4.3 N m
80 N m
2.5 N m

questions.explanation: Perpendicular distance = 0.25 × sin 30° = 0.125 m, so the turning effect = 20 × 0.125 = 2.5 N m.

questions.stem: A robot vacuum moves 1.1 m east and then 1.6 m north, each along a straight line. What is the magnitude of its displacement from its starting point?

A ray of light passes from air into a transparent liquid. The incident ray makes an angle of 40.0° with the surface of the liquid and the refracted ray makes an angle of 55.0° with the surface. The speed of light in air is 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. What is the speed of light in the liquid?

Predict first. Monochromatic light of wavelength 600 nm is incident normally on a single slit, and the diffraction pattern is viewed on a distant screen. The slit width is then reduced from 0.20 mm to 0.10 mm. How does the central maximum change?

options.text: It becomes half as wide and less intense, as it is an image of a slit that is now half as wide.
It is unchanged, as both slits are far wider than 600 nm, so neither diffracts significantly.
It becomes twice as wide and less intense, as less light passes and is spread over a wider angle.
It becomes twice as wide, with unchanged peak intensity, which depends only on the source.

questions.stem: Three forces act at a point. Which set of magnitudes could keep the point in equilibrium?

options.text: 2 N, 3 N and 6 N
5 N, 7 N and 11 N
4 N, 4 N and 9 N
3 N, 5 N and 9 N

questions.explanation: 11 N is less than 5 N + 7 N = 12 N, so the three can form a closed triangle at suitable angles. Their resultant can be zero.
